# [CS057] Possible Typosquatted Dependency (dependency-typosquatting)

A required module path is one or two characters away from a well-known module.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Severity** | HIGH |
| **Category** | Supply Chain & Provenance |
| **CWE** | [CWE-1357](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/1357.html) |
| **OWASP** | A03:2025 |
| **Auto-Fix supported** | No |

## Why It Matters in Go

Vulnerability scanners only know published advisories, so a freshly registered look-alike module, or a module name that never existed until someone registered it after seeing it suggested, shows zero vulnerabilities. The check compares requirements with about 300 widely used modules, counting transpositions and look-alike characters as one edit. Modules under organization-controlled domains, of your own account, or under allowed_prefixes are not compared.

## Vulnerable / Problematic Example

```text
require github.com/gin-gonlc/gin v1.10.0
```

## Safe / Idiomatic Go Pattern

```text
require github.com/gin-gonic/gin v1.10.0
```

## Configuration & Suppression

Disable the rule for the whole module in `.codexsentinel.yaml`:

```yaml
rules:
  disabled: [dependency-typosquatting]
```

Change its severity:

```yaml
rules:
  severity_overrides:
    dependency-typosquatting: low
```

Suppress one reviewed finding on its line, with the reason:

```go
//codex:ignore dependency-typosquatting -- <reason>
```

Or ignore it under a path in `.codexsentinel.ignore`:

```text
internal/legacy/** dependency-typosquatting
```
